self-attention.name: self-attention
self-attention.definition: A content-dependent weighted mixture whose queries, keys, and values come from the same sequence.
self-attention.explanation: Each query row scores key rows, row softmax converts scores to source-position probabilities, and the weighted sum retrieves value rows. Scores are scaled by the inverse square root of head width to control predictable dot-product growth. Self-attention exchanges information across positions, unlike a feed-forward layer that transforms positions independently. Multiple heads repeat the calculation on feature slices. The operation does not by itself enforce sequence direction; a causal mask supplies that restriction for autoregressive language modeling.

causal-mask.name: causal mask
causal-mask.definition: A restriction that permits position i to attend only to positions j where j is not later than i.
causal-mask.explanation: During parallel next-token training, future tokens are present in the input tensor. Without a causal mask, a representation can read information about the target it must predict, producing misleadingly low loss. Mask forbidden attention scores before row softmax so their source-position probability and score gradient are zero. These probabilities choose input positions; they are distinct from the later probability distribution over predicted token classes. The diagonal is allowed because position i contains the current input token while its target is token i+1.

gradient-check.name: gradient check
gradient-check.definition: A comparison between an analytical derivative and a numerical finite-difference estimate.
gradient-check.explanation: For a scalar objective and one input element, central difference estimates the derivative by subtracting the objective at a small negative perturbation from the objective at the same positive perturbation, then dividing by twice the perturbation. It is slow but useful on tiny deterministic fixtures. Smooth inputs, suitable precision, and combined absolute and relative tolerances matter. This chapter sums attention outputs times a fixed upstream matrix to create a derivative probe; that probe is not a model loss or next-token cross-entropy. Causal invariance and shape tests complement numerical derivatives because agreement alone cannot prove the intended information flow.
